title: Open-base locality of structural and geometric-fibre conditions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, let $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ be an arbitrary open cover, and let $C,F,X$ be schemes over $S$, and let $p:C\to S$, $q:F\to S$, $j:F\to C$ and $r:C\to X$ be morphisms over $S$, with $q=p\circ j$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Fix $d,e\geq0$. The following structural conditions hold globally if and only if they hold after restriction to every $S_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]: $p,q$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], their nonempty fibres have pure dimensions $d,e$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], $j$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $q$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The same locality assertion holds for any chosen subset of these conditions. The condition that $j(F)$ lies in the relative smooth locus of $p$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is also local in this sense. More generally, let $P$ be any rule assigning a proposition to diagrams $F_\Omega\to C_\Omega\to X_\Omega$ of schemes over algebraically closed fields, invariant under isomorphisms of such diagrams. The condition that $P$ holds on every chosen algebraic-closure geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] of $(j,r)$ is equivalent to its holding for the restriction over every $S_i$. This last assertion requires no invariance of $P$ under field extension: for a point $s\in S_i$ use the same residue-field closure on $S$ and $S_i$. There is no finiteness assumption on the cover or on $S$, and empty schemes, empty marking, nonproper curves and nonseparated curves are allowed.

source.place: Tags 01TP (definition-finite-presentation), 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), 01U3 (definition-flat), and 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion); open-target locality of quasi-compactness of the map and its diagonal and etaleness, as in the existing locality nodes. Geometric-fibre identity over an open neighbourhood; returned Step 14, agent-written assembly.

proof.text: For an open $V\subset S$ put $Y_V=Y\times_SV$ for $Y=C,F,X$. Identify $Y_V$ with the open subscheme $a_Y^{-1}(V)\subset Y$, where $a_Y$ is its structure map: a pair of maps $T\to Y$, $T\to V$ agreeing over $S$ is exactly a map $T\to Y$ whose composite to $S$ factors through $V$. The factor is unique by the open-factorization lemma. This verifies the fibre-product universal property and gives the identification with both projections. The restrictions of $j,r$ are therefore their actual restrictions to these opens; $q=p\circ j$ gives $j^{-1}(C_V)=F_V$. At $y\in Y_V$, open restriction preserves the local ring and the induced local ring map: neighbourhoods contained in $Y_V$ are cofinal among neighbourhoods of $y$. In particular $\kappa_V(s)=\kappa_S(s)$ for $s\in V$.

source.place: Open restriction and fibre-product universal property; agent-written identification using the cited definitions and open-factorization lemma

proof.text: Apply the local-ring identification of Step 1 to $p$ and $q$. At a point above $S_i$ the local homomorphism defining flatness is the same before and after restriction. By the definition of a flat morphism, global flatness implies flatness of every restriction; conversely, each point of $C$ or $F$ lies above some $S_i$, so flatness of all restrictions gives flatness at that point. This proves the flatness equivalence separately for $p$ and $q$.

source.place: definition-flat (flatness at a point and flatness everywhere)

proof.text: Let $a:Y\to S$ be either $p$ or $q$. Finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Global finite presentation restricts to each $S_i$ by the base-change assertion (3) of the qcqs permanence node. Conversely, assume every $a_i:Y_i\to S_i$ is finitely presented. Target-open locality gives local finite presentation of $a$, and quasi-compact target locality gives quasi-compactness of $a$. For quasi-separatedness put $D=Y\times_SY$ and $D_i=D\times_SS_i$. The $D_i$ are an open cover of $D$ by Step 1. The restriction of $\Delta_a:Y\to D$ to $D_i$ is $\Delta_{a_i}:Y_i\to Y_i\times_{S_i}Y_i$: maps to either displayed product are pairs of maps to $Y_i$ with the same structural map, so the product identification and the equality of the two diagonals follow from uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property. Each $\Delta_{a_i}$ is quasi-compact. Apply quasi-compact target locality to $\Delta_a$ on this cover. Its quasi-compactness is precisely quasi-separatedness of $a$. Thus all three defining conditions of finite presentation hold.

source.place: definition-finite-presentation; locality of local finite presentation and quasi-compactness, including application to the diagonal

proof.text: The opens $C_i=p^{-1}(S_i)$ cover $C$, and the inverse image of $C_i$ under $j$ is $F_i$ by Step 1. Apply clause (1) of the closed/finite/etale target-locality node to $j:F\to C$ and this cover: $j$ is a closed immersion exactly when all $j_i$ are. Apply clause (3) of the same node to $q:F\to S$ and the cover $(S_i)$: $q$ is etale exactly when all $q_i$ are. These applications impose no conditions on $p$ or $r$.

source.place: Open-target locality for closed immersions and etaleness, as recorded by the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Fix $s\in S_i$ and first take $T=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. For each $Y=C,F,X$, the projection $(Y\times_SS_i)\times_{S_i}T\to Y\times_ST$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is given by the same map to $Y$ and the unique factorization of $T\to S$ through $S_i$; each composite has the original projections, hence is the identity by the fibre-product universal property. Thus the entire ordinary fibre over $s$ is unchanged, rather than merely an open part of it. The induced homeomorphism identifies irreducible components and chains of irreducible closed subsets in each component, so pure dimension $d$ for $C_s$ and $e$ for $F_s$ is unchanged. Since every $s$ belongs to some $S_i$, this gives both implications of the pure-fibre-dimension assertions. Empty fibres agree on both sides and impose no condition.

source.place: Fibre-product universal property and the definition of pure dimension; agent-written comparison

proof.text: Interpret the relative smooth locus as the set of points admitting an open neighbourhood on which the structural morphism is smooth. For $c\in C_i$, if $p$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood $W\subset C$ of $c$, clause (a) of the smooth-restriction node makes $W\cap C_i\to S_i$ smooth. Conversely, if $p_i$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood $W_i\subset C_i$ of $c$, then $W_i$ is open in $C$ and clause (b), with target open $S_i\subset S$, makes $W_i\to S$ smooth. The two smooth loci therefore agree on $C_i$. For each $f\in F$ choose $i$ with $q(f)\in S_i$; then $j(f)\in C_i$ and the assertion $j(f)$ lies in the smooth locus is identical for $j$ and $j_i$. This proves locality of the image-containment condition without requiring the marking to be nonempty or $p$ to be globally smooth.

source.place: definition-smooth and lemma-smooth-characterize; open restriction and composition with a target open immersion

proof.text: For the chosen algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\kappa(s)}$ at $s\in S_i$, use the same residue-field closure on $S$ and $S_i$ via Step 1. Repeat the explicit mutually inverse maps of Step 5 with $T=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. They are isomorphisms over this fixed $\Omega$ for $F,C,X$. They intertwine $j_\Omega,r_\Omega$: both composites have the same projections to the original schemes and to $T$, so uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property makes them equal. The hypothesis on $P$ therefore identifies its truth on the two fibre diagrams. Global truth restricts to each $S_i$, and truth on every restriction implies global truth by choosing an $i$ containing each $s$. No change of field is made. Steps 2--6 established each structural equivalence independently, so taking a conjunction over any chosen subset gives exactly the stated subset assertion. All arguments use a covering only to locate a single point or apply the cited arbitrary-cover locality; for $S=\varnothing$ all schemes over $S$ are empty and the same statements are vacuous (the structural morphisms and their diagonals are empty isomorphisms).
